data.narrative:
Terrestrial Energy is a public-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $280M to date. The nuclear energy sector comprises a modest peer universe of 10 comparable entities: 3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private firms. The five most active private peers are Oklo, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

A peer-median valuation approach is not applicable in this instance. The nuclear energy sector lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within similar valuation tiers to generate a reliable median multiple. Only one same-stage peer was identified, falling below the three-datapoint minimum threshold needed for methodological rigor. Attempting to broaden the filter to the full 10-firm sector cohort would introduce substantial heterogeneity across stage and scale, rendering cross-sectional multiples unreliable for Terrestrial Energy's specific profile.

The narrow and dispersed peer set presents a material constraint on triangulation. Alternative methods—such as DCF analysis, precedent transactions within nuclear, or stage-adjusted benchmarking against the three public comparables—would be required to support a valuation range. Without application of a primary quantitative method, no point estimate can be responsibly derived from available data. Further analysis should incorporate management guidance on capital deployment and technology-to-revenue timelines to narrow valuation uncertainty in this nascent, capital-intensive sector.
